summary: A 46-ft Pacific Coast Steel tower erected by a CCC crew in 1936 on Woody Mountain, NRHP-listed 1988 and still standing; no public visit route found.

facts.design: 46 ft steel tower with 7x7 ft cab, provided by Pacific Coast Steel, one of relatively few towers that company supplied

access.note: Coconino National Forest, administered by the U.S. Forest Service (Peaks Ranger District cooperator). No public visitor information, trail or rental listing was found in the sources read; check with the Forest before visiting.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: 1936 build, 2001 NHLR registration, USFS agency, 46 ft (14.0 m) height. The NRHP nomination PDF itself was unavailable (HTTP 403 on the NARA S3 copy), so the design and NRHP details rest on the NPGallery metadata, Wikidata and the NHLR page. Staffing status is not given by any source read; the only staffing evidence is the 1912 timeline entry. A Facebook group post says the tower has not been regularly staffed for some time, but it is undated and was not used. Living New Deal also credits the CCC with the 1936 build; not fetched. Access is unknown; the brief's unknown stands. Sources differ on the tree-stand start (register 1910, timeline 1912 stationing) but they are not contradictory. Photos on Wikidata (Woody Mountain Lookout Tower (full).jpg) have no fetched URL and were not added. The 1936 current-tower date is inferred from the register's wood-tower span ending 1936 'when the current tower was built', not from a stated build field. The timeline has no entries after 1936.
